# Project conventions

## Architecture
- Use Next.js App Router, React and TypeScript. `/participants`, `/mood` and `/timer` are real routes; `/` redirects to participants. Do not restore hash routing or direct local-file opening.
- Keep route entries and metadata in `src/app`, route-specific UI in each route's private `_components`, reusable UI in `src/components`, behavior in `src/hooks`, persistence and notifications in `src/providers`, domain types in `src/types`, and pure domain helpers in `src/lib`. Keep storage/audio adapters explicit and browser APIs client-side.
- Style components with Tailwind CSS v4 utilities. Keep shared utility recipes in `src/components/ui/styles.ts` and brand tokens, Tailwind import, minimal base rules and animation keyframes in `src/app/globals.css`; configure its PostCSS plugin in `postcss.config.mjs`. Do not restore legacy stylesheets or custom component CSS. Runtime inline styles are limited to calculated ring/progress/overlay geometry and animation variables. Preserve the Infomil blue/orange palette and French UI copy, labels, prompts and notifications.

## Behavior and safety
- Render participant names as React text, never injected HTML. Use accessible native controls, visible focus, responsive paginated lists and reduced-motion support, including GIF pause behavior.
- Restore/normalize `standup.team.v2` in the team provider, migrate legacy preferences on the same origin, and tolerate unavailable storage with an in-memory fallback and visible notice. Never promise automatic transfer of `file://` data to HTTP origins.
- Wait for persistence hydration before route guards redirect. Require at least one present teammate and a numbered 1–4 mood for every present teammate before creating a session; absent teammates must never enter the lineup. Attendance/mood edits invalidate it.
- Calculate countdowns from deadlines, not interval counts. Clean up timers, event listeners and audio on unmount. Do not persist running countdowns or speaking progress, auto-advance speakers, or let shortcuts intercept native controls/dialogs.
- Shuffle only eligible unfinished participants; lock the active speaker once their turn starts, including while paused, and ensure a changed order when possible.

## Assets
- Treat `public` as generated by `scripts/prepare-assets.mjs` through `npm run assets`, `predev` and `prebuild`; hard links may share source content, so never edit generated assets directly.
- Keep root `infomil-logo.svg` and `mood-meter.html`: asset publishing requires them. Publish browser images/catalogue only, never PowerPoint sources or internal reports/metadata.
- Leave the existing PowerPoint downloader/exporter and `mood-meters` corpus unchanged unless explicitly requested. After an export, rerun assets and rebuild/redeploy. Account for 888 decks (~9.6 GB) against hosting limits; never bypass licensing or access restrictions.

## Setup and validation
- See [README](../README.md) for setup, commands, migration and deployment details. Node >=20.9 is the app minimum; the configured TypeScript test runner requires Node >=22.6.
- Use package scripts for dev/build/start/assets/lint/typecheck/test. Do not claim checks passed until executed and results reviewed; hand deferred validation back explicitly. Follow task-specific terminal restrictions.
